title: 67% of Americans Change Their Personality at Work
paragraphs: Are you the same person at work as you are at home? For many Americans, the answer seems to be no, according to a new survey.
The survey was conducted by The Harris Poll for Express Employment Professionals, a staffing company. It asked American job seekers and hiring managers about the role of personality in the workplace.

It found that 67% of job seekers have changed some parts of their personality to fit in with their workplace culture. In addition, 63% said that their personality at work is very different from who they are in their daily lives.

Younger workers were the most likely to adjust their personalities. Around 80% of Gen Z job seekers said they had changed their personality at work, compared with 69% of millennials, 59% of Gen X and 50% of baby boomers and older workers.

Most job seekers believe that adapting is necessary. In fact, 86% said they consider it a core professional skill, and 83% said that employees who cannot or will not adjust may not stay at their company for long.

Many people also believe that personality affects how others judge their work. About 91% of job seekers and 94% of hiring managers said personality shapes how people view an employee's performance. Furthermore, 99% of hiring managers said that having a positive or friendly personality can help people move up in their careers more quickly.
However, many people do not think this is completely fair. More than half of job seekers, 56%, said their personality has nothing to do with their work or their ability to do their job.
Bob Funk Jr., the CEO of Express Employment International, said workplace culture should set expectations for how people treat each other, but it should not decide who people have to be.
